blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: When an authorization policy blocks an agent's tool call, the audit log should name the facts that forced the decision and nothing more. For an executable policy over an enumerable context space this minimal sufficient reason can be computed exactly, so an explanation is scored against ground truth rather than a proxy for it. We use that exactness to ask what a model can learn from a verifier that has no error in it. The explainer sees one request and one decision, never the policy, and has thirty turns in which it may call the policy on altered requests and ask whether a candidate set of facts is sufficient. Frontier models find the exact reason about half the time with the tools alone, and one sentence telling them to shrink the answer lifts Haiku 4.5 from 58% to 75%. A 4B model fine-tuned on 2000 traces of the deletion algorithm reaches 92% on the policy it was trained on. Teacher kind is what moves this: at matched data size the algorithm-taught student leads the frontier-taught one in all three training seeds, and the two arms never overlap. What the student learns is a fixed schedule of sufficiency checks, and the schedule does not travel. On three public policies it never saw, its answers stay sufficient (94%) and stop being minimal (48%), while Haiku under the same sentence is exact on all 47 episodes. Reinforcement learning from the exact reward leaves held-out accuracy where it was and inverts the strategy, from probing the policy to spending the entire budget on sufficiency checks. The oracle made the effect of training legible, but it did not make training better.

blocks.en:
Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards works where a verifier exists, and the field is now
asking what happens when the verifier is a rubric, a judge, or a heuristic that only approximates the
objective ( Helff et al., 2026 ; Mahmoud et al., 2026 ) . We take the other end of that question and
suppose the verifier is exact. What can a model learn from it, and what can it not?

blocks.en:
Explaining a decision of an executable authorization policy is a task where exactness is available
and the answer is non-trivial. An agent asks to send a file to an external
domain, and the policy blocks it. A useful audit entry names the facts that forced the block, say the
target domain and the absence of elevated authorization, and leaves out the facts that did not
matter. In the formal explanation literature this is an abductive explanation or prime implicant ( Shih et al., 2018 ; Ignatiev et al., 2019 ) , a subset of the request’s features whose values
entail the decision under every completion of the rest, with no proper subset that does. We call it
a minimal sufficient reason (MSR). For a policy over an enumerable context space an oracle can enumerate every MSR of every
decision, so a cited reason set is scored against ground truth rather than a proxy for it.

Four results follow. First, frontier accuracy does not follow model tier, and one sentence of
instruction moves it. On 120 shared
episodes with both tools, Haiku 4.5 reaches the exact MSR on 58% and Sonnet 5 on 50%, against 16% for Gemini Flash-Lite. Opus 5 is exact on all 21 episodes it did not refuse, but that

Flash-Lite to 43%. Sonnet does not move, for a reason unrelated to what it cites. On 55 of 120 episodes it
answers in prose instead of the required action format and the harness ends the episode empty; where
it commits it is exact 94% of the time. Its score is a
format-compliance number, and we report it as one (Section 3 ).

frontier-taught student and trained with a group-relative baseline against a reward in which exact
minimality dominates, the student does not get more accurate on held-out episodes ( + 3 +3 points, p = 0.80 p=0.80 ).

reward and starvation at the reward ceiling both appear with the verifier held exact, which places them in the reward’s shape rather than in its error (Section 6 ).

blocks.en:
GlassGate is an executable authorization policy for an agent gateway ( Debenedetti et al., 2025 ; Debenedetti et al., 2024 ) . A request is a context x x over
ten categorical features: the tool being called (twelve values), the scope level, the target domain,
three content flags for personal, credential and financial data, the caller’s authorization level and
role, the declared intent, and a count of prior violations. The product of the domains is 124,416 124{,}416 contexts, and the policy is a fixed function g : X → { allow , block } g:X\to\{\text{allow},\text{block}\} .
Because X X is enumerable, every claim below about sufficiency is decided by evaluating g g , not by
sampling. Five public policies are the held-out domains: a load-balancer policy in OPA, two Kubernetes
Gatekeeper constraints (seccomp profiles and container limits), and two Cedar policies (a streaming
service and a tax-preparation service). They have three to ten features and run on the same oracle
machinery. The students were scored on the OPA and Cedar policies, the frontier models on all five. All episodes are stratified over the decision and over MSR size.

blocks.en: 6 Reinforcement learning from the exact reward

blocks.en:
The exact oracle gives a process reward with no error in it, and the question is whether RL against it
can push the frontier-taught student toward the algorithm-taught one. We warm-start from Frontier-148, since Alg-2000 sits at the reward ceiling and yields no
within-group variance to learn from, and train with REINFORCE and a group-relative baseline over four
rollouts per context on fresh contexts, for 25 steps. Table 1 gives the held-out result and Appendix B the training-time evaluations.

能够把边疆学徒推向算法学徒。 我们从Frontier-148开始,因为Alg-2000坐在奖励的上限上,没有
用REINFORCE和4个以上的集团相对基线进行学习和训练
根据新情况逐个推出,共25个步骤。 表1列出了所搁置的结果和附录B的培训时间评价。

blocks.en:
Our first reward weighted sufficiency and recall above exact minimality and precision, with small

blocks.en: 7 Related work
blocks.zh: 7 相关工作

blocks.en:
Geng et al. (2025) have LLMs recover a hidden program, formal language or equation by
querying it, and find that models plateau under passive observation and improve when allowed to
intervene. Yin et al. (2025) benchmark the same protocol across 96 hidden functions, and Wei et al. (2025) fine-tune an 8B model on traces from a teacher with access to the hidden function,
the closest precedent for training the querier. Our setting shares the premise and differs in the object. Their
explainer hypothesises a whole function; ours explains one decision and is scored exactly against
every minimal sufficient reason of that decision, and we train the querier rather than only
prompting it. Mayne et al. (2025) show self-generated counterfactuals are valid but not minimal, the failure our check tool makes measurable. The protocol is query learning ( Angluin, 1988 ; Weiss et al., 2018 ) : decide is a membership query, check a sufficiency query, and unlike L ∗ there is no equivalence oracle.

The minimal sufficient reason is the abductive explanation of Ignatiev et al. (2019) , the prime implicant of Shih et al. (2018) , and the sufficient reason of Darwiche and Hirth (2020) , whose term we adopt; Marques-Silva and Ignatiev (2022) argue formal XAI should deliver it. Query-based methods for related objects predate LLMs: Anchors ( Ribeiro et al., 2018 ) finds
high-precision sufficient conditions of a black box by sampling, Blanc et al. (2021) give
query-efficient algorithms with guarantees, and the deletion procedure we use as teacher is the
standard extractor for minimal unsatisfiable cores ( Junker, 2004 ) . Recent work computes these for black-box vision models by query, Xing and Lagniez (2026) for point clouds and Hoarau et al. (2026) at the concept level. Those are
algorithms, and our question is whether a language model can be taught to run one. An exact oracle replaces the faithfulness proxies of Atanasova et al. (2023) and Chen et al. (2024) , which Gur-Arieh et al. (2026) show do not measure faithfulness.

blocks.en: 8 Limitations
blocks.zh: 8 限制

blocks.en:
Alg-148 and Frontier-148 have three training seeds each (Appendix B ); every other arm has one,
so intervals elsewhere are over episodes. Three seeds is also the floor for a seed-level test, since
complete separation of 3 against 3 gives an exact permutation p p of 0.10, so the teacher-kind claim
rests on the within-seed paired tests and the non-overlap. One student size and one base model were
trained. GlassGate is a single hand-written policy, and the student loses to Haiku on all three public policies it was
scored on. Sonnet’s numbers are bounded by a harness rule, two malformed replies end the episode, that
no other model triggered; a different rule would raise Sonnet and change nothing else. The oracle needs
an enumerable context space, bounding the setting to categorical policies.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 9 结论

blocks.en:
With the verifier exact, every result above is measured against ground truth. The frontier finds a
minimal sufficient reason about half the time with the tools alone and three quarters once
instructed. An algorithm can teach a 4B model to match it where a frontier model cannot, but only on
the gate it was taught on; off it, sufficiency travels and minimality does not. An exact reward
changed the strategy in both RL runs and moved accuracy in opposite directions. In the supervised and
RL results alike, training installed the shape of a procedure without the judgment inside it, and the
exact verifier is what let us tell the two apart.
